novelty_flags.one_line: The cited TMLR paper is titled “Identification of Average Outcome under Interventions in Confounded Additive Noise Models,” not the title given in the core; correct the named comparator before retaining theorem-level comparisons.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 1 (sanity reduction)
novelty_flags.one_line: This proposition intentionally restates published Gaussian and parentless mean special cases, so it must remain a regression corollary rather than a claimed novel result.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and the ANM class
soundness_flags.one_line: The class never requires the structural maps to be Borel measurable, although their measurability is necessary for the SCM laws, residual map, and pushforward functional to be defined.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1
soundness_flags.one_line: For arbitrary standard-Borel subsets E and EY, C_b^2(E×EY), derivatives, and the stated local-polynomial construction have no specified meaning; impose Euclidean-domain regularity or define an extension/restriction convention.

source_verification_receipts.version: Transactions on Machine Learning Research, October 2025
source_verification_receipts.locator: title page; Theorem 2 and Appendix A.3, pp. 6 and 16–17
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published title is “Identification of Average Outcome under Interventions in Confounded Additive Noise Models”; Theorem 2 gives a Gaussian AOI identification criterion and Eq. (17) recovers a shifted treatment mechanism.

The paper proves identification results for additive multivariate-Gaussian SCMs with unobserved confounders; Theorem 2 concerns disentangled conditional average treatment effects in the symmetric ANM.
The paper identifies joint intervention effects from observational and singleton-intervention distributions under nonlinear continuous additive Gaussian-noise SCMs.

source_verification_receipts.version: pre-publication manuscript corresponding to Econometrica 81(6), 2205–2268; journal DOI 10.3982/ECTA10582
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The counterfactual-distribution operator has a uniform limit theory and exchangeable-bootstrap validity for the paper's regression-based estimators.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Borel measurability of every f_i and f_Y to the ANM class, and state that all treatment/outcome state spaces are Euclidean domains or explicitly define C_b^2 and local-polynomial estimators through smooth ambient extensions.

Make the exact-cover theorem account explicitly for supplied regimes with T_r=I: either prohibit them in R or allow their observed outcome laws to satisfy the outcome-cell clause, then formulate the matching necessity witness for that enlarged information set.

Promote the full-law theorem and exact-cover frontier as the only novelty claims; move the Gaussian/parentless proposition to an unnumbered regression corollary and correct the TMLR comparator title throughout.

recommended_next_step: Return to Stage -1 to repair measurability/domain semantics and the Elahi citation, then reassess the exact-cover frontier with all supplied regime information included.
